cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Law reform is necessary because society changes and the law must adapt to address new situations, correct injustices and keep pace with technology and social values

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: The Law Commission is an independent body established by the Law Commissions Act 1965 with a duty to keep the law under review and recommend reform

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: The Law Commission produces reports with draft Bills; however, implementation depends on Parliament — only around 70% of Law Commission recommendations are eventually implemented, often with significant delay

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Parliamentary reform through Acts of Parliament is the primary method of law reform; Parliament can change any area of law and is not bound by previous legislation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Judges reform the law through the development of precedent — the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal can depart from previous decisions to update the law (e.g. the Supreme Court in Montgomery changed the law on informed consent)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: The 1966 Practice Statement allowed the House of Lords (now Supreme Court) to depart from its own previous decisions when it appears right to do so

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Technology creates new legal challenges: cybercrime (Computer Misuse Act 1990), data protection (UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018), online harassment and the regulation of social media

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: The Online Safety Act 2023 places duties on platforms to protect users from harmful content, including illegal content and content harmful to children

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Artificial intelligence raises legal questions about liability, intellectual property, privacy and the potential need for new regulatory frameworks

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Human rights reform remains debated: proposals to replace the HRA 1998 with a Bill of Rights raise questions about the future of Convention rights in UK law

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Contemporary issues include: the impact of Brexit on legal certainty and retained EU law, reform of the criminal justice system (court backlogs, legal aid), and debates about policing practices

cards.front: Recall a key point about Law Reform & Contemporary Issues
cards.back: Pressure groups, media campaigns and public opinion all influence law reform — Parliament responds to public concern, as seen with changes to stalking law and domestic violence legislation

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — law reform & contemporary issues?
cards.back: 1. For Law Reform & Contemporary Issues questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Law Reform & Contemporary Issues 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
